deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no derivation. It continues the 'Register über die Kraft der Magnetstäbe', the register of the strength of the magnet bars begun on the previous page. It is a dated log, from late August to mid-October, of a measured strength (effectively the magnetic moment, in Gauss's own working units) for eight numbered bars, columns 1–8.

Each row is a date: Aug 27, 28, 29, 31; Sept 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 13, 18, 26, 29, 30; Oct 1, 2, 3, 9, 14. Several values stacked under one date are successive measurements on that day. They are separated by marginal notes on what was done to the bars:
- 'Dch' (meaning uncertain) is written above the Aug 28 values for bars 1–4.
- 'nach Erwärmung' (after warming), Sept 4, bars 5–6.
- 'mit 4 Stäben gestrichen' (stroked with 4 bars), Sept 12/13, bars 3–5.
- 'mit 8 Stäben gestr[ichen]' (stroked with 8 bars), Sept 30, bars 5–8.
- 'nach der Trennung' / 'nach Trennung' (after separation of the bars from the bundle), Sept 30.

What the numbers show (my reading of the data):
- Repeated stroking raises the moments. For example, bar 1 goes 1411.9 → 1838.5 on Aug 27, then 1927.0 → 2055.9 on Aug 28.
- Between strokings the moments decay slowly. Bar 5 falls from 2490.8 (Sept 6) to 2474.8 (Sept 10), a loss of about 0.64%.
- Warming changes the moment. Bar 5 reads 2450.8 before and 2421.8 after warming on Sept 4, a fall; bar 6 rises, 2384.5 → 2404.5.
- Stroking with 8 bars instead of 4 lifts bars 5–8 to their highest values. Bar 5 goes from 2561.3 (Sept 26) to 2774.9 (Sept 30). Bar 7 reaches about 3000 to 3019 by Oct 14.
- Bars that sat together in a bundle can show transient, strongly altered values just after separation. On Sept 30 the readings were 1770.1, 1033.0, 1185.7 and 1147.0 for bars 1–4. Bar 8 read 1224.9, between 2884.2 before and 2877.4 after. These recover on re-measurement.
- By Oct 1–3 the bars settle: roughly 2210–2277 (bar 1), 2083–2112 (bars 2–4), about 2770 (bars 5–6), about 3016 (bar 7) and about 2851–2860 (bar 8).
- The margin note 'B 2669.18 30 Sept' records an auxiliary bar B.

Purpose: this is the practical, experimental side of Gauss's absolute magnetic measurements of the 1830s at Göttingen. He wanted bars with the largest and most stable magnetic moment. The data compare magnetisation procedures (double touch with bundles of 4 or 8 bars), the effect of temperature, and the decay over time. The next page continues the log and reduces moments to a standard bar weight of 400 g.

There is no mathematics to reconstruct beyond reading the table.
errors: No computational errors are possible to assess; the page is raw measurement data.
The Sept 2 entries for bars 3–4 (1869.8, 1835.6) are struck through and re-entered under Sept 3. This is a correction of the date line, not an error in value.
Bar 8's 'nach Trennung' value of 1224.9 (Sept 30) is anomalous next to 2884.2 and 2877.4. It is probably a genuine transient effect after separation from the bundle, or a misread, rather than a slip.

results.what: Log of magnetic moments of 8 bar magnets under different magnetising treatments (stroking with 4 vs 8 bars), warming, separation from bundles, and time decay
results.modern_name: Experimental magnetometry / magnetisation of permanent magnets by the method of double touch; secular decay and thermal sensitivity of magnetic moment
results.usually_credited_to: Magnetisation by touch: Michell, Canton, Aepinus (18th c.); absolute moment measurement: Gauss (1832–33)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine laboratory register belonging to Gauss's well-documented magnetic work of the 1830s. It contains no mathematical result.

checkable.asserts: Relative decay of bar 5 from Sept 6 to Sept 10 is about -0.0064 (-0.64%).
Stroking with 8 bars raised bar 5's moment by a factor of about 1.083.
Stroking with 8 bars raised bar 7's moment by a factor of about 1.103.
Warming reduced bar 5's moment by about 1.2% on Sept 4.
